# Step 7: apply the principles

Goal: every decision you make with this library follows the frameworks behind it. Each framework below has its rules (never break them), a decision procedure (ask in order; the first answer that fits decides) and the checks that catch a miss. The same frameworks are shown to people, in short, at the bottom of the library pages.

## Which framework governs what

| You are choosing | Read |
| --- | --- |
| A token in `color.*`, `state.*`, `spectrum.*`, `set.*` | [Colour](#colour) |
| A token in `space.*`, `size.*`, `breakpoint.*` | [Spacing](#spacing) |

<a id="library"></a>

## How the library works

Full framework: How the library works (docs/how-it-works.md).

**Rules**

- Look comes only from tokens; a view, page or content file never carries a class name, style prop, CSS file or raw value.
- Components are sealed (no className or style props). Change them by the seam ladder: prop or variant, slot, context attribute, theme, custom part inside a template, then a reviewed core change.
- Screens are data: a template manifest names layouts and regions; content JSON fills them; the renderer maps content to layouts, compounds and fundamentals.
- Tiers depend downward only: tokens <- fundamentals <- compounds <- layouts <- templates. A fundamental never imports a compound.
- Never edit a generated file (tokens.colour.json, tokens.space-shape.json, css/tokens.css, tokens/generated/*, agent/*, generated content schemas).

**Decide**

1. Search packages/core/agent/index.json for an existing component, block type, layout or template before writing anything.
2. Pick the lowest tier that meets the need: a fundamental if it is universal, a compound if it arranges fundamentals for one need, a layout for named regions of a screen.
3. If nothing fits, take the first seam on the ladder that works; a custom part lives in your template as {template}.{Part}.

**Check:** `npm run check:views`, `npm run check:content`, `npm run agent:index:check`

<a id="constraints"></a>

## The owner’s design rules

Full framework: Design constraints (docs/brief.md#design-constraints).

**Rules**

- Never a one-sided accent border (border-left stripe) on a card, button, callout or nav item; use a fill, tint, full outline, icon or badge.
- A binary setting is a Switch, never a Button used as an on/off toggle.
- Inner segments of a stacked or segmented bar are square; only the outer ends of the whole bar may round.
- Pad once at the right interior level (one or two levels below the visual wrapper), never all around a wrapper or per leaf; scroll regions bleed to the surface edge with the scrollbar at the edge; never clip a focus ring.
- One component variant per need: no second pattern where one already does the job.
- Notifications auto-dismiss; manual dismiss only when the person must read it.

**Decide**

1. Before adding an accent, choose fill, tint, full outline, icon or badge, in that order of preference.
2. Before adding a variant, search agent/components/{Name}.json for an existing prop that covers the need.
3. Before adding padding, find the wrapper that owns the visual edge and pad the first content level inside it; keep the scroll container itself unpadded.

**Check:** `npm run check:clipping`, `npm run check:views`

<a id="presets"></a>

## Presets

Full framework: Token presets (docs/foundation.md#token-presets-q70).

**Rules**

- A preset is a saved choice per category: colour, type, icons, space, shape, material. A global preset names one per category.
- Built-in presets are read-only; user presets are saved beside them (design-library.presets) and sync across tabs.
- Templates inherit the global preset; a template never hard-codes a category choice.
- Choose at run time with @design-library/core/presets (applyGlobalPreset, applyCategoryPreset); change defaults at build time through the token config files.

**Decide**

1. The product owns this repository look: change the theme (config file, npm run tokens).
2. The app needs another built-in option: apply a category or global preset at run time.
3. A person wants to keep their choice: saveCategoryPreset or saveGlobalPreset.

**Check:** `npm run tokens:check`, `npm run agent:index:check`

<a id="colour"></a>

## Colour

Full framework: The colour model (docs/foundation.md#colour-model).

**Rules**

- Components read semantic roles only (color.text, color.bg-raised, color.border-control, state.*); never p.* primitives.
- Status meaning only through color.status.{info,success,warning,danger,neutral}.{fg,bg,border,fill,on-fill}, always with an icon or words: never colour alone.
- spectrum.* and set.* only for the purpose in their $extensions["org.design-library"].purpose (charts, identity), never for function.
- Change colour in packages/core/tokens/colour.config.json, then npm run tokens; never edit tokens.colour.json.
- Contrast: text 4.5:1 and non-text 3:1 in light, dark and both contrast levels; tokens:check refuses a theme that misses one.

**Decide**

1. Is it text, a surface, a line or a control fill? Use the matching color.text*, color.bg*, color.border* or color.bg-control role.
2. Does it mean a status? Use color.status.* and add an icon or words.
3. Is it the brand action, link, focus or selection? It already reads the accent; don’t add another.
4. Is it a category in a chart or an identity? Use a declared set.* or spectrum.* with its purpose.
5. None fits: add a role through the colour config, never a literal.

**Check:** `npm run tokens`, `npm run tokens:check`

<a id="spacing"></a>

## Spacing

Full framework: Spacing in the foundation plan (docs/foundation.md#space-and-shape-options).

**Rules**

- One 4 px base unit; components read roles (space.stack-pair, stack-item, stack-group, stack-section, inline-*, inset-*, gutter, margin-page), never a scale step.
- Space inside a group is never larger than the space around it.
- The parent owns space: gap and padding on the container (Stack, Cluster, Grid gap props); never margins set by a sibling position.
- Geometry never moves on hover, focus or loading: borders are always there, transparent at rest.
- Targets are at least size.target (44 px), or size.target-dense in dense contexts.

**Decide**

1. Related items (label and value): stack-pair. Items in a list: stack-item. Groups: stack-group. Sections: stack-section.
2. Side by side: inline-pair, inline-item, inline-group by the same levels.
3. Inside a surface: inset-* at the first content level, not on the wrapper.
4. Need a whole product denser or looser? Change the space option (compact, normal, loose, extra-loose), never single values.

**Check:** `npm run tokens:check`, `npm run check:clipping`

<a id="visual-noise"></a>

## Visual noise

Full framework: Craft skills applied (docs/foundation.md#craft-skills-applied).

**Rules**

- Every mark (border, divider, fill, shadow, icon, colour, line of text) must carry information nothing else carries.
- Cue order, cheapest first: space, alignment, type, tone, border, shadow. One cue per meaning.
- Type is a cue: hierarchy comes from the type roles (type.*), not from extra colour, boxes or icons.
- At most one enclosure per boundary; no box inside a box.
- Transient affordances (drag handles, hover actions, customise cues) appear only while their state is active.
- Approved components are never restyled as a side effect of another change.

**Decide**

1. Can space or alignment group it? Stop there.
2. Else, can type weight or size? Then tone (a fill step). Then a full hairline. A shadow only if it floats.
3. Already inside an enclosure? Do not add another; separate with space.

**Check:** `npm run check:parts`, `npm run check:views`

<a id="elevation"></a>

## Elevation and layering

Full framework: Materials and backgrounds (docs/materials.md).

**Rules**

- Six levels: -1 sunken, 0 canvas, 1 raised, 2 chrome, 3 floating, 4 modal (packages/core/principles/elevation.json).
- Tone first, shadow second, edge last. shadow.raised for anchored floating surfaces; shadow.overlay for free floating and modal. No shadow at rest on content or chrome.
- z-index only as var(--layer-*) or a c.<part>.layer token aliasing one; never a number, never an inline zIndex.
- Popups open in the top layer (popover attribute); dialogs as modal dialog elements; the layer token is only the fallback order.
- A component ordering its own parts with layer.behind or layer.raised sets isolation: isolate on the holder.

**Decide**

1. Pick the level from the ladder by what the surface does, then the layer by the "Choosing a layer" questions (elevation.json, printed below in the guide); the first yes decides.
2. Hidden behind something? Find the ancestor that starts a stacking context and move the thing to the top layer; never raise the number.

| Level | Name | Material | Layers | Use | Never |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| -1 | Sunken | MT2 sunken | `layer.base` | A region set into the page that holds other things. One tone step down; no shadow, no outline. | A shadow or an outline: a well is lower, not a box. |
| 0 | Canvas | MT1 canvas | `layer.base` | The page itself. Most content needs nothing above it. color.bg; no panels around whole regions. | Panels around whole regions: enclosure noise. |
| 1 | Raised | MT3 raised, MT4 tint, MT5 control fill | `layer.base`, `layer.raised (inside a component)` | Something set onto the page that a person reads or works in. One tone step up; a hairline only where tone can’t separate; never a shadow at rest. | A shadow at rest: content doesn’t float. |
| 2 | Chrome | MT6 chrome | `layer.sticky` | A bar that stays put while the page scrolls under it. layer.sticky; frosted when the global setting is on; hairline only while content is under it; no shadow at rest. | A shadow at rest, or floating material for a docked bar. |
| 3 | Floating | MT7 floating | `layer.popover`, `layer.toast`, `layer.tooltip` | Something that opens over the page without blocking it. Top layer; shadow.raised when anchored to a trigger, shadow.overlay when free; frosted when on; never glass on glass. | Glass on glass: a floating surface inside another is solid. |
| 4 | Modal | MT9 scrim + MT8 modal | `layer.overlay`, `layer.dialog` | Something that blocks the page until it’s answered, over a dimmed page. layer.overlay scrim + layer.dialog surface; shadow.overlay; always solid. | Frosted: the scrim already separates and the content is text. |

**Choosing a layer** (first yes decides)

1. Does it need to be above anything at all? Content stays at layer.base in source order; nothing raises itself to win.
2. Does it stay while content scrolls under it? It’s chrome: layer.sticky, inside its own scroll region.
3. Does it open from a trigger or float free? Open it in the browser’s top layer (the popover attribute, or a modal dialog element); its layer token (layer.popover, layer.toast, layer.tooltip) is only the fallback order.
4. Does it block the page? A modal dialog element, with layer.overlay for the scrim and layer.dialog for the surface.
5. Does a component order its own parts? layer.behind and layer.raised, with isolation: isolate on the element that holds them, so the order never leaks.
6. Still hidden behind something? Find the ancestor that starts a stacking context (a transform, filter, opacity below 1, isolation or a z-index) and move the thing to the top layer or to the layout’s overlay. Never a bigger number.
7. Write z-index only as var(--layer-*) or a component token that aliases one (c.<part>.layer). npm run check:layers fails on a number, an inline zIndex, a component stacking token that aliases no layer, and inside layers without isolation, in core, the library, templates and the example app.

**Check:** `npm run check:layers`, `npm run check:materials`

<a id="materials"></a>

## Materials

Full framework: Materials and backgrounds (docs/materials.md).

**Rules**

- A component names its material (canvas, sunken, raised, tint, control, chrome, floating, modal, scrim, veil); tokens decide how it is painted.
- The content layer (canvas, sunken, raised, tint, control) is always solid; only chrome and floating may be frosted.
- Frosted is one global setting (data-material="frosted" or "solid" on the root); never per component.
- Never glass on glass: a floating surface inside another is solid.
- Reduced transparency, more contrast, forced colours and print are solid. Blur radius never animates.
- Chrome, floating and modal surfaces carry data-material and data-elevation (the add-on seam).

**Decide**

1. A page or region: canvas; rails and wells: sunken; a card or field: raised or control fill; the current item: tint.
2. A bar content scrolls under: chrome. A popup or free toolbar: floating. A blocking surface: modal over the scrim. Controls over media: veil.

**Check:** `npm run check:materials`

<a id="motion"></a>

## Motion

Full framework: Motion and transitions (docs/motion.md).

**Rules**

- Components read motion roles (duration.quick, change, move, move-far, shared; easing.standard, enter, exit, linear), never the private scale (fast, medium, slow).
- Every visual value change (fill, border colour, shadow, opacity) eases at duration.change (200 ms); nothing jumps.
- Content present in both states morphs (same wrapper, shared element) instead of disappearing and reappearing.
- Zero latency where a person drives a value (typing, arrow-key steps, drags, sliders): no transition on that value (packages/core/motion/zero-latency.json).
- With reduced motion travel snaps and fades stay; never transition: all; never a literal duration or curve.

**Decide**

1. Does the person drive the value directly? No transition on it.
2. Is it a colour, fill, border, shadow or opacity change? duration.change with easing.standard.
3. Does something travel or resize? duration.move or move-far; arriving uses easing.enter, leaving easing.exit.
4. Is the same thing on both sides of a view change? A shared-element morph (duration.shared).

**Check:** `npm run check:motion`

<a id="ui-states"></a>

## States

Full framework: Craft skills applied (docs/foundation.md#craft-skills-applied).

**Rules**

- Every committed change is confirmed where it was made for at least duration.confirm-min.
- Each state has one owner level (app, view, section, component, field) and one look: loading, saving, success, error, empty.
- Views and sections load with shimmer skeletons; one bottom notification pill, one line, at most three.
- Errors keep the input and always offer a recovery (Retry, Revert).
- Empty states live in the content’s own wrapper and say why and what to do.

**Decide**

1. Field-level change: the field shows pending, confirmed or failed (useCommit).
2. Whole view loading: a skeleton in the view, keeping the old view until the new one is ready.
3. A result of an action elsewhere: one notification pill that auto-dismisses.
4. Nothing to show: EmptyState inside the list or region, with the next action.

**Check:** `npm run typecheck`

<a id="perceived-performance"></a>

## Waiting

Full framework: Loading in the foundation plan (docs/foundation.md#loading).

**Rules**

- Classify the wait: instant, responsive, waiting or long, and give the matching feedback.
- Never block or lose input during a wait; keep the old view until the new one is ready.
- One honest status; never a silent wait.
- Indicators wait duration.indicator-delay before showing and stay at least duration.indicator-min.

**Decide**

1. Under about 100 ms: no indicator. Up to about a second: a local indicator after the delay. Longer: progress with words. Very long: progress plus a way to keep working.

**Check:** `npm run typecheck`

<a id="ui-copy"></a>

## Words

Full framework: Craft skills applied (docs/foundation.md#craft-skills-applied).

**Rules**

- Words come from content or props, never hard-coded in a component.
- Sentence case, plain words, curly apostrophes; buttons are verbs that say the result.
- Errors say what happened and how to fix it; never blame the person.
- One name per thing across the product (the glossary).
- Every icon-only control has an accessible name, shown by Tooltip.

**Decide**

1. Label: the noun or the verb, two to four words.
2. Error: what happened, then the fix, in one or two short sentences.
3. Empty state: why it is empty, then the action.

**Check:** `npm run check:content`

<a id="visual-representation"></a>

## Showing information

Full framework: Visual representation (docs/visual-representation.md).

**Rules**

- Run the reasoning chain in docs/visual-representation.md before choosing text, an icon, a picture, an illustration, media or a chart.
- Show as is when accuracy, verbatim words or the content itself must be preserved.
- Every visual carries a text alternative; charts never mislead (zero baselines for bars, honest scales).
- Chart categories read set.* or spectrum.* with their declared purpose; status never by colour alone.
- Inner bar segments stay square.

**Decide**

1. Follow the agent procedure in docs/visual-representation.md (The chain as an agent procedure) and its Agent checklist.

**Check:** `npm run check:content`
